rationale:
Evidence from the last race (iteration 1, entityR2A): score 446, up from 88. Oval finishes 15/20 (mean progress 0.92, max_error 0.026, rms 0.008). S-bend finishes 3/20 (progress 0.79, max_error 0.061). Slalom finishes 0/20 (progress 0.35). Every failure is off_track, and max_error reaches the 0.06 m limit (body_width/4 term is only 0.036, so the limit is fixed at 0.06 m). Line-loss events average about 1 per run. Steering_oscillation is moderate (0.23 to 0.37), so the loop is not jittering. The robot tracks well near the line and then runs wide on bends it cannot turn back from. Moving the sensors forward to y=0.06 and narrowing the spread to +/-0.03 m clearly helped (iteration 0 to 1), so I keep that layout.

Hypotheses: (1) On the s-bend and slalom, the robot still enters bends at too much speed, so it overshoots the line before steering responds. (2) Turning authority is limited by yaw inertia, which is set by mass*(body_length^2+body_width^2)/12. A shorter body lowers it and lets the robot turn back faster. (3) kp=4 with kd=0.6 leaves a little room: oscillation is low, so a stronger proportional response with more damping should cut max_error without causing jitter.

Changes: base_speed 1.0 to 0.9 (less overshoot on bends; the oval still has time margin because it finished in about 2.0 s, and the 3 s limit allows some slack). kp 4.0 to 4.5 for a stronger corrective turn. kd 0.6 to 0.8 to damp the higher gain; the s-bend oscillation of 0.37 leaves room. body_length 0.18 to 0.14 to cut yaw inertia about 20 percent (mass*(L^2+W^2)/12 falls from about 0.0034 to 0.0029 with W=0.12). Sensor layout, sensor size, wheel geometry, mass, body_width, ki and line_loss are unchanged, so the effect of the change is attributable to speed, gains and inertia.

Expected result: fewer off_track endings on the s-bend and slalom (max_error below 0.06), slalom progress rising above 0.5, and oval completion holding. Risk: lower base_speed may push completion time near 3 s on the longer tracks.

Hypotheses to test next: if off-track is still on tight bends, the next step is a wider sensor spread (+/-0.04) or a larger sensor (0.016). If the robot now completes but is slow, raise base_speed back toward 1.0 with the higher kd.

Measurements to check: completion and completion_time per track, max_error and line_loss_events (are they lower at the same bends?), and steering_oscillation (is the higher kp and kd causing jitter?).
